texts: One script tag and one element: a live 3D avatar on any page, 8 at a time, idling as it appears

Two lines of HTML put a live 3D avatar on a web page. The element holds its frame back until the idle has rendered, so the avatar appears standing naturally on Mixamo, VRM and other rigs alike. The write-up follows one snippet from the tag to that frame, then covers pinned versions with integrity hashes, reduced motion and a budget of 8 live avatars per page.

altText: Three 3D avatars standing side by side on a dark blue background, each rendered live by its own agent-3d element in the same relaxed idle pose: a woman in a purple top and leggings, a character in a cropped top, yellow trousers and round pink glasses, and a man in a white T-shirt, light jeans and green trainers

editor.summary: Every claim in the article verifies against source files or live pages, and the structure meets the Article standard: one real run, ten sections, real code and tables, four inline images, a partners section with exact designations, and a Try it section. The promo post leads with the mechanism, the title carries the 8-avatar number, and the cover shows the real product with accurate alt text, so this ships as is.
